tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

schema.name: ScheduleWakeup
schema.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.content:
1	# 04 · User flow and state machine
2	
3	Behaviour of the subscribe flow, from plan list to confirmed. Q-numbers refer to `03-open-questions.md`.
4	
5	## Terms
6	
7	- **Open order**: the last order this browser created, kept in storage that every tab shares and that outlives the tab (Q37). It holds orderId, `paymentUrl`, plan and market. It is cleared when the server reports `paid`, `failed` or 404.
8	- **Attempt marker**: written to shared storage just before `POST /v1/orders` and removed once the response arrives (Q39).
9	- **Retry point**: the place where failures land and where an explicit "Pay" or "Try again" lives. That's Review when `reviewStep` is on. When it's off, it's Plans with the chosen plan preselected and a banner (Q38).
10	- **Gate**: the check that every path into CreatingOrder passes first (see below).
11	
12	## Invariants
13	
14	1. **One order per attempt.** Only an explicit click at the retry point creates an order. Reload, Back, return, polling and a second tab never create one. While an open order is `pending` or `requires_action`, no new order is created in any tab: it's resumed instead (Q30, Q37).
15	2. **Trust: server > stored context > URL query.** Order status and identity come only from the API. Stored context beats the URL for plan, market and locale. The URL is used only when nothing is stored (Q7). `cancelled=1` is a hint that the server must confirm.
16	3. **Polling errors never show "payment failed".** Only `status: failed` from `GET /v1/orders/{id}` means failed. Network errors, 5xx, 401 and 404 have their own states.
17	4. **Every state has an exit.** Each non-terminal state has at least one action the user can take or a timeout. No state has only a spinner.
18	5. **Context survives redirects.** Plan, market, locale, `utm_*` (and orderId after payment) are in every `returnUrl` (Q7).
19	6. **State is re-derived on every show.** Each state runs its "on enter" step on first load, on reload and when Back restores the page from the back-forward cache. Disabled buttons are re-enabled when the page is restored. Nothing on the page is trusted until on-enter has run again.
20	
21	## Happy path
22	
23	```
24	Entry ─/v1/me─▶ Plans ─select─▶ StartingEid ─▶ [eID] ─▶ EidCallback ─/v1/me─▶ Review
25	  ─Pay─▶ Gate ─▶ CreatingOrder ─▶ [payment] ─▶ PaymentReturn ─▶ Polling ─paid─▶ Confirmed
26	```
27	
28	Shortcuts:
29	- An identified user (Entry `/v1/me` 200) skips eID. Select → Review, or Gate if `reviewStep` is off.
30	- With `reviewStep` off, the flow skips Review: Verifying → Gate (Q32).
31	
32	## Gate (before every order)
33	
34	1. **Open order present** → `GET /v1/orders/{id}`.
35	   - `pending` or `requires_action` → **Resume**: no new order.
36	   - `paid` → Confirmed.
37	   - `failed` or 404 → clear it, continue.
38	   - 401 → IdentityLost.
39	   - 5xx or network → retry point + error. Pay disabled until the check succeeds.
40	2. **Attempt marker present** (a reload or crash during CreatingOrder) → clear it and show "Your last attempt didn't finish" at the retry point. Pay needs one more click. The lost order never got a `paymentUrl`, so it can't be paid (Q39).
41	3. **`GET /v1/me`** → `activeSubscription` → Account. 401 → StartingEid (context kept). 5xx or network → retry point + error, no order. 200 → CreatingOrder.
42	
43	**Resume** = the retry point shows only "Continue payment" (reuses `paymentUrl`) and "Check status" (→ PaymentReturn). Pay and "Change plan" are hidden.
44	
45	## States
46	
47	| State | On enter | Exits |
48	|---|---|---|
49	| **Entry** | `GET /v1/me` | 200 + `activeSubscription` → **Account**. 200 → Plans (identified). 401 → Plans (anonymous). 5xx/network → Plans (anonymous, checked again after eID) |
50	| **Plans** | Show API plans for the market, matched to CMS cards (Q8). Market off by flag → root. Open order `pending` → Resume banner | Select: identified → Review (or Gate if `reviewStep` off). Anonymous → StartingEid |
51	| **StartingEid** | `POST /v1/identity/sessions` with returnUrl + context. Button disabled | 201 → redirect to `redirectUrl`. 429 → **RateLimited**. 400, 5xx or network → **StartError** |
52	| **RateLimited** | Countdown from `Retry-After` (fallback 30 s, Q35). Polite `aria-live` | Countdown ends → "Try again" enabled → StartingEid. "Change plan" → Plans (shows Resume if there's an open order) |
53	| **StartError** | "Can't start eID right now" | "Try again" → StartingEid. "Change plan" → Plans |
54	| **EidCallback** | Read `status` from the query. Every exit uses `history.replace`, so the callback URL never stays in history: Back or reload can't re-run it or re-send `identity_completed` (07) | `ok` → Verifying. `cancelled` → **EidFailed(cancelled)**. `expired`, missing or unknown → **EidFailed(expired)** (Q36) |
55	| **EidFailed** | Message for the reason | "Try again" → StartingEid (same context). "Change plan" → Plans |
56	| **Verifying** | `GET /v1/me` | 401 → **OtherBrowser**. 5xx/network → **VerifyError**. 200 + orderId in context (from IdentityLost) → **PaymentReturn** for that order, checked before the subscription. 200 + `activeSubscription` → **Account**. 200 → Review (or Gate if `reviewStep` off) |
57	| **VerifyError** | "We couldn't confirm your identity" | "Try again" → Verifying. "Start again" → StartingEid |
58	| **OtherBrowser** | "Continue in the browser where you started" (Q7) | "Start again here" → StartingEid using the context from the URL |
59	| **Review** | Fetch `GET /v1/plans` again (the price shown here is binding, Q23). Run Gate step 1 for display: an open `pending` order → Resume | Plan missing from API → Plans + notice. Plans fetch fails → error + retry, Pay disabled. "Pay" (disabled on click) → Gate. "Change plan" → Plans |
60	| **CreatingOrder** | Write the attempt marker. `POST /v1/orders` `{planId, market, returnUrl}` | 201 → save the open order, clear the marker → redirect to `paymentUrl`. 401 → StartingEid (context kept, Q17). 409 `already_subscribed` → **Account** (Q10). Other 409 → Gate once more (Q41). 400 `invalid_plan` → Plans + notice. 5xx → retry point + error. Network/no response → retry point + error, marker kept, no automatic retry (Q34) |
61	| **PaymentReturn** | orderId from stored context, else from the URL. None → Plans | One `GET /v1/orders/{id}`: `failed` + `cancelled=1` → **PaymentFailed(cancelled)**. `failed` → **PaymentFailed(declined)**. `paid` → Confirmed. Anything else → Polling |
62	| **Polling** | `GET /v1/orders/{id}` every 2 s for 20 s, then every 5 s, stop at 3 min (Q9). Status in a polite `aria-live` region | `paid` → Confirmed. `failed` → PaymentFailed(declined). `requires_action` → redirect to `actionUrl` (once per poll cycle). `pending` → keep polling. 20 s → "Still confirming" text. 3 min → **Unconfirmed**. 5xx/network → keep polling, show "Connection issue, still checking". 401 → **IdentityLost**. 404 → **OrderNotFound** |
63	| **PaymentFailed** | Open order cleared. Retry point + banner: cancelled ("Payment cancelled") or declined ("Payment was declined") (Q31) | "Try again" → Gate (**new order**). "Change plan" → Plans |
64	| **Unconfirmed** | "We'll confirm shortly", order id shown. Open order kept | "Check again" → one GET, then the same exits as Polling. "Go to account" → Account. No new order offered |
65	| **IdentityLost** | "Verify to see your payment status", order id shown. Open order kept (Q33) | "Verify" → StartingEid, returnUrl carries the orderId → Verifying → PaymentReturn |
66	| **OrderNotFound** | "We can't find this order", order id shown. Open order cleared | "Back to plans" → Plans. "Go to account" → Account |
67	| **Confirmed** | Order id, plan, trial note if any. `purchase` fires once per orderId (Q20), params taken from the open order before it's cleared (07). Then open order and context cleared. On reload the open order is gone: no trial note | Terminal. "Go to account" → Account. Reload → GET again; `paid` stays Confirmed |
68	| **Account** | Redirect to `ACCOUNT_URL` (Q10) | Terminal (outside the flow) |
69	
70	Trial shown on Review and Confirmed only if `trialEligible` and the plan is Standard or Premium (Q12).
71	
72	## Mock scenarios → path
73	
74	| Scenario | Path | Ends in |
75	|---|---|---|
76	| `happy` | Full happy path. Polling sees `paid` within ~3 s | Confirmed |
77	| `identity_cancelled` | StartingEid → eID → `?status=cancelled` | EidFailed(cancelled) → retry |
78	| `identity_slow` | Same as happy. The 8 s wait happens on the provider page, where we have no state | Confirmed |
79	| `rate_limited` | StartingEid → 429, `Retry-After: 30` | RateLimited → retry after countdown |
80	| `already_subscribed` | Anonymous: Verifying sees `activeSubscription`. Identified: Entry sees it. Gate step 3 and the order 409 also catch it | Account |
81	| `not_trial_eligible` | Happy path. Review shows the full price, no trial | Confirmed |
82	| `payment_declined` | PaymentReturn → `pending` → Polling → `failed` after ~1 s | PaymentFailed(declined) → new order on retry |
83	| `payment_slow` | Polling passes 20 s ("Still confirming") and sees `paid` at ~45 s | Confirmed |
84	| `payment_requires_action` | The mock sends the user to the challenge on its own, then returns. If polling sees `requires_action` (the user left the challenge), redirect to `actionUrl`. Approve → `paid`. Decline → `failed` | Confirmed / PaymentFailed(declined) |
85	| `api_500` | Plans render from the build. Entry `/v1/me` 500 → anonymous. StartingEid 500 → StartError. If already past eID: Verifying → VerifyError, Gate → retry point + error, polling → "Connection issue" → Unconfirmed after 3 min | StartError / VerifyError / Unconfirmed, never PaymentFailed |
86	
87	Cases not tied to a scenario:
88	
89	| Case | Trigger in mock | Ends in |
90	|---|---|---|
91	| eID expired | Wait > 5 min on the eID page, or reuse a completed session | EidFailed(expired) |
92	| Payment cancelled | "Cancel" on the pay page → `&cancelled=1`, order `failed` | PaymentFailed(cancelled) |
93	| Back from payment page | Browser Back to Review (fresh load or restored from the back-forward cache), order `pending` | Invariant 6 → Resume (same order) |
94	| Double tap on Pay | Two clicks | One request (in-flight guard in the handler; button `aria-disabled`, 08) |
95	| Reload during CreatingOrder | F5 before the 201 | Gate step 2 → "last attempt didn't finish". No payable duplicate |
96	| Second tab while paying | Tab A on the payment page or polling, tab B opens Plans/Review | Tab B shows Resume. No second order |
97	| Session expired on the payment page | Pay → return → poll 401 | IdentityLost → eID → PaymentReturn (mock: 404 → OrderNotFound, because every mock eID creates a new customer) |

165	
166	`transaction_id` = `orderId` [D]. `value` = Review price in euros, `0` if trial was shown: **our estimate**, the server never returns an amount (Q4). `currency` = plans `currency` [M]. Fires once per `orderId` (Q20).

168	## Normalized error model
169	
170	One adapter, `toApiError(response | thrown)` → `{status, code, message, retryAfterSec?}`. UI never reads raw bodies (Q18).
171	
172	1. `{errors:[{code, message}, …]}` → first entry.
173	2. `{error: "message"}`, non-JSON or empty body → `code` from status: 400 `invalid_request`, 401 `unauthenticated`, 404 `not_found`, 409 `conflict`, 429 `rate_limited`, 5xx `internal_error`.
174	3. fetch rejects or times out → `{status: 0, code: 'network'}`.
175	4. 429 → `retryAfterSec` from `Retry-After` (seconds), else 30 (Q35).
176	
177	Then `kind` from endpoint + status + code [M]. An unknown code takes the kind of its status. 429 outside identity counts as `server` (Q42).
178	
179	| Status / code | Kind | State in 04 (depends on caller) |
180	|---|---|---|
181	| 0 `network` | `network` | Entry → Plans (anonymous) · StartingEid → StartError · Verifying → VerifyError · Review plans fetch → error + retry, Pay disabled · Gate (any step) → retry point + error · CreatingOrder → retry point, marker kept, no auto retry (Q34) · PaymentReturn → Polling · Polling → keep polling, "Connection issue" |
182	| 5xx | `server` | Same as `network`, except CreatingOrder: retry point + error, marker cleared |
183	| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Entry → Plans (anonymous) · Verifying → OtherBrowser · Gate step 3, CreatingOrder → StartingEid, context kept · Gate step 1, Polling → IdentityLost · PaymentReturn → Polling (which then shows IdentityLost) |
184	| 409 `already_subscribed` | `alreadySubscribed` | Account (Q10) |
185	| 409, other code | `conflict` | CreatingOrder → Gate once more (Q41) |
186	| 400 `invalid_plan` | `invalidPlan` | CreatingOrder → Plans + notice |
187	| 404 on `/v1/orders/{id}` | `orderNotFound` | Polling → OrderNotFound · Gate step 1 → clear open order, continue |
188	| 429 on identity | `rateLimited` | StartingEid → RateLimited, countdown `retryAfterSec` |
189	| other 4xx (incl. 404 elsewhere) | `badRequest` | StartingEid → StartError · Review plans fetch → error + retry · Gate, CreatingOrder → retry point + error. Logged (our bug) |
190	
191	No kind maps to PaymentFailed. Only `status: failed` from `GET /v1/orders/{id}` does (04, invariant 3).

217	## What the docs give us, and what they don't
218	
219	- Six events, names fixed by marketing ("keep names exactly as written") [D]. Happy path only: no event for a cancel, decline, error or timeout.
220	- Only `purchase` has params: `transaction_id`, `value`, `currency` [D]. Nothing for the other five (Q20).
221	- "UTM parameters should survive until `purchase`" [D]. No storage rule, and the flow leaves our origin once or twice: eID, then payment (plus `actionUrl` on `requires_action`). Return can land in another browser (Q7).
222	- No consent mechanism (Q5). GA4 in the EU needs prior consent for analytics cookies.
223	- `purchase` fired in the browser misses every user who never comes back from payment, and can fire twice (reload, second tab, second browser).
224	- The order API returns no amount, currency or trial flag (Q4). `value` is our estimate.

226	## Module
227	
228	One pure module, `analytics.ts`:
229	
230	- `track(event, params)`: typed map of the six events → their params. Unknown event = type error.
231	- Adds the common params, checks consent, applies the once-rules, then `dataLayer.push`.
232	- Components and state handlers call `track` on the transitions below. Nothing else touches `dataLayer`.
233	- Unit-tested: params per event, once-rules, consent gate, no personal data.

279	
280	Never sent: `customerId`, eID data (none is exposed anyway, Q15), `sessionId`, `paymentUrl`, `actionUrl`, `redirectUrl`, `returnUrl`, error messages. `orderId` is pseudonymous and required by marketing as `transaction_id`. A unit test asserts the param whitelist per event.

282	## UTM capture and storage
283	
284	**Capture** [A]: on Entry, read `utm_*` from the landing URL. A new landing with any `utm_*` replaces the whole set (last campaign wins). A landing without UTMs keeps a stored set. Other query params are ignored (`gclid` etc.).
285	
286	**Carry**: two (three with `actionUrl`) cross-origin redirects, maybe into another browser (Q7).
287	
288	| Where | Before consent | After consent |
289	|---|---|---|
290	| Memory (current page, client-side navigation) | yes | yes |
291	| `returnUrl` query, eID and payment (Q7) | yes: URL, not storage (Q5) | yes |
292	| `sessionStorage` (same tab, after a redirect) | no | yes |
293	
294	Trust order as 04 invariant 2: stored > `returnUrl` query. On return, the app reads UTMs from the query only when nothing is stored. Without consent, UTMs exist only in the URL, so they survive the redirects but not a manual reload of a page without them.
295	
296	`returnUrl` keeps the standard `utm_*` names. Side effect: the return page view re-states the campaign, so GA4 doesn't credit the eID or payment provider as a referral. Still needed from marketing: eID and payment domains in GA4 "unwanted referrals" (Q47).
297	
298	Limits: UTMs add to `returnUrl` length, and the provider/API limit is not documented (02). UTMs reach the eID and payment providers in the URL; they hold no personal data.
299	
300	## Consent
301	
302	Assumption Q5: GTM Consent Mode v2, basic mode (no Google tags before consent). CMP vendor unknown.
303	
304	| | Before a decision | Granted (`analytics_storage`) | Denied or withdrawn |
305	|---|---|---|---|
306	| Consent default | `gtag('consent', 'default', {analytics_storage, ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization: 'denied'})` before GTM loads | `update` by the CMP | stays denied |
307	| App events | Queued in memory, current page only | Queue flushed, then pushed live | Queue dropped, nothing pushed |
308	| UTMs | Memory + URL | + `sessionStorage` | Memory + URL. Withdrawal clears our keys |
309	| `purchase` guard | not written | `localStorage` | not written. Withdrawal keeps existing keys (orderId only, no personal data), so a re-grant + reload can't send `purchase` twice |
310	| GA cookies (`_ga`) | none | set by GA | none |
311	
312	- Queued events not flushed before a redirect or reload are lost. Accepted (Q5): a user who decides after eID shows `identity_completed` without `plan_viewed`/`plan_selected`/`identity_started`, so the top of the funnel is undercounted.
313	- Return in another browser: no CMP cookie there, so the banner shows again on the callback page; events queue until the decision.
314	- The flow never waits for, or depends on, consent or GTM. Functional storage (open order, attempt marker, Q37) is not analytics and needs no consent.
315	- Advanced mode (cookieless pings) is a Legal decision (Q5).
316	- The CMP and GTM count against LCP, INP and CLS on Plans, not the JS size budget (08).

439	
440	A convenience built from the API notes in `docs/02-api-notes.md`. Where the notes are silent, the mock had to make a choice. The real services may differ, so treat anything you rely on here as an assumption to write down.
441	
442	Everything is in memory. Restart the server, or `POST /__mock/reset`, to start clean.

444	## Choosing a scenario
445	
446	A scenario decides how the mock behaves. Pick one in any of these ways. The first match wins:
447	
448	1. The `x-scenario` request header.
449	2. A `?scenario=` query parameter. This also sets a `nl_scenario` cookie, so the choice sticks for later requests, including page navigations to the fake providers.
450	3. The `nl_scenario` cookie, which you can also set by clicking a scenario on the landing page (<http://localhost:4010>).
451	4. Otherwise `happy`.
452	
453	When you create an identity session or an order, the mock remembers the scenario in force at that moment and uses it for the provider pages that follow.

456	| --- | --- |
457	| `happy` | Everything works. Payment is confirmed about 3 seconds after the customer pays. |

459	| `identity_slow` | The eID provider takes about 8 seconds to answer. |

464	| `payment_slow` | Payment is confirmed about 45 seconds after the customer pays. |
465	| `payment_requires_action` | The provider asks for an extra authentication step before it confirms payment. |

# 04 · User flow and state machine

Behaviour of the subscribe flow, from plan list to confirmed. Q-numbers refer to `03-open-questions.md`.

## Terms

- **Open order**: the last order this browser created, kept in storage that every tab shares and that outlives the tab (Q37). It holds orderId, `paymentUrl`, plan and market. It is cleared when the server reports `paid`, `failed` or 404.
- **Attempt marker**: written to shared storage just before `POST /v1/orders` and removed once the response arrives (Q39).
- **Retry point**: the place where failures land and where an explicit "Pay" or "Try again" lives. That's Review when `reviewStep` is on. When it's off, it's Plans with the chosen plan preselected and a banner (Q38).
- **Gate**: the check that every path into CreatingOrder passes first (see below).

## Invariants

1. **One order per attempt.** Only an explicit click at the retry point creates an order. Reload, Back, return, polling and a second tab never create one. While an open order is `pending` or `requires_action`, no new order is created in any tab: it's resumed instead (Q30, Q37).
2. **Trust: server > stored context > URL query.** Order status and identity come only from the API. Stored context beats the URL for plan, market and locale. The URL is used only when nothing is stored (Q7). `cancelled=1` is a hint that the server must confirm.
3. **Polling errors never show "payment failed".** Only `status: failed` from `GET /v1/orders/{id}` means failed. Network errors, 5xx, 401 and 404 have their own states.
4. **Every state has an exit.** Each non-terminal state has at least one action the user can take or a timeout. No state has only a spinner.
5. **Context survives redirects.** Plan, market, locale, `utm_*` (and orderId after payment) are in every `returnUrl` (Q7).
6. **State is re-derived on every show.** Each state runs its "on enter" step on first load, on reload and when Back restores the page from the back-forward cache. Disabled buttons are re-enabled when the page is restored. Nothing on the page is trusted until on-enter has run again.

## Happy path

```
Entry ─/v1/me─▶ Plans ─select─▶ StartingEid ─▶ [eID] ─▶ EidCallback ─/v1/me─▶ Review
  ─Pay─▶ Gate ─▶ CreatingOrder ─▶ [payment] ─▶ PaymentReturn ─▶ Polling ─paid─▶ Confirmed
```

Shortcuts:
- An identified user (Entry `/v1/me` 200) skips eID. Select → Review, or Gate if `reviewStep` is off.
- With `reviewStep` off, the flow skips Review: Verifying → Gate (Q32).

## Gate (before every order)

1. **Open order present** → `GET /v1/orders/{id}`.
   - `pending` or `requires_action` → **Resume**: no new order.
   - `paid` → Confirmed.
   - `failed` or 404 → clear it, continue.
   - 401 → IdentityLost.
   - 5xx or network → retry point + error. Pay disabled until the check succeeds.
2. **Attempt marker present** (a reload or crash during CreatingOrder) → clear it and show "Your last attempt didn't finish" at the retry point. Pay needs one more click. The lost order never got a `paymentUrl`, so it can't be paid (Q39).
3. **`GET /v1/me`** → `activeSubscription` → Account. 401 → StartingEid (context kept). 5xx or network → retry point + error, no order. 200 → CreatingOrder.

**Resume** = the retry point shows only "Continue payment" (reuses `paymentUrl`) and "Check status" (→ PaymentReturn). Pay and "Change plan" are hidden.

## Analytics `purchase`

`transaction_id` = `orderId` [D]. `value` = Review price in euros, `0` if trial was shown: **our estimate**, the server never returns an amount (Q4). `currency` = plans `currency` [M]. Fires once per `orderId` (Q20).

## Normalized error model

One adapter, `toApiError(response | thrown)` → `{status, code, message, retryAfterSec?}`. UI never reads raw bodies (Q18).

1. `{errors:[{code, message}, …]}` → first entry.
2. `{error: "message"}`, non-JSON or empty body → `code` from status: 400 `invalid_request`, 401 `unauthenticated`, 404 `not_found`, 409 `conflict`, 429 `rate_limited`, 5xx `internal_error`.
3. fetch rejects or times out → `{status: 0, code: 'network'}`.
4. 429 → `retryAfterSec` from `Retry-After` (seconds), else 30 (Q35).

Then `kind` from endpoint + status + code [M]. An unknown code takes the kind of its status. 429 outside identity counts as `server` (Q42).

| Status / code | Kind | State in 04 (depends on caller) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 `network` | `network` | Entry → Plans (anonymous) · StartingEid → StartError · Verifying → VerifyError · Review plans fetch → error + retry, Pay disabled · Gate (any step) → retry point + error · CreatingOrder → retry point, marker kept, no auto retry (Q34) · PaymentReturn → Polling · Polling → keep polling, "Connection issue" |
| 5xx | `server` | Same as `network`, except CreatingOrder: retry point + error, marker cleared |
| 401 | `unauthenticated` | Entry → Plans (anonymous) · Verifying → OtherBrowser · Gate step 3, CreatingOrder → StartingEid, context kept · Gate step 1, Polling → IdentityLost · PaymentReturn → Polling (which then shows IdentityLost) |
| 409 `already_subscribed` | `alreadySubscribed` | Account (Q10) |
| 409, other code | `conflict` | CreatingOrder → Gate once more (Q41) |
| 400 `invalid_plan` | `invalidPlan` | CreatingOrder → Plans + notice |
| 404 on `/v1/orders/{id}` | `orderNotFound` | Polling → OrderNotFound · Gate step 1 → clear open order, continue |
| 429 on identity | `rateLimited` | StartingEid → RateLimited, countdown `retryAfterSec` |
| other 4xx (incl. 404 elsewhere) | `badRequest` | StartingEid → StartError · Review plans fetch → error + retry · Gate, CreatingOrder → retry point + error. Logged (our bug) |

No kind maps to PaymentFailed. Only `status: failed` from `GET /v1/orders/{id}` does (04, invariant 3).

## Requests to backend, by launch impact

1. **`market` on `POST /v1/orders`**, or derive it server-side, and reject a plan not sold in that market. Otherwise wrong VAT is charged (Q1).
2. **Prod CORS** for the `www` origin with credentials, and cookie `SameSite`/domain. Without it no API call works from the static site (Q40).
3. **Confirm the provider return contracts**: `returnUrl` in both bodies, eID `status`, payment `orderId` and `cancelled`, `actionUrl`. The whole flow is built on mock behaviour (Q6).
4. **Amount, currency and trial flag on the order** (POST and GET), and what a trial order charges. Needed for the price shown vs charged and GA `value` (Q4).
5. **`Idempotency-Key` on `POST /v1/orders`** (allowed in CORS), and 409 while the customer has a pending order. Prevents duplicate charges (Q19, Q37, Q39).
6. **`state` param on the eID callback**. Prevents login CSRF (Q7).
7. **One error shape and a code catalogue**, including 401 on `/v1/me` (Q18, Q28).
8. **Failure reason on `failed` orders**, so cancel and decline are told apart without `cancelled=1` (Q6, Q31).
9. **`Retry-After` on every 429** (Q35).
10. **Order settle time SLA or a push channel** (Q9).
11. **Auth session lifetime** (Q17).
12. **`planKey` and `trialDays` on plans** (Q11, Q12).
13. **Document `currency`, the `activeSubscription` shape, the `plans` wrapper, the order `status` field and success status codes** (Q26, Q43).
14. **Error mapping for 409 codes other than `already_subscribed`, and 429 outside identity** (Q41, Q42).
# 07 · Analytics

The GA4 events the flow sends through GTM, what they carry, and when they may be sent. Transitions refer to `04-user-flow-state-machine.md`. Q-numbers refer to `03-open-questions.md`. Quality checks are in `08-quality.md`.

Marks: **[D]** in `docs/04-analytics-notes.md` · **[A]** our rule.

Out of the thin slice (PLAN.md). Server-side `purchase` and extra events are cut (PLAN.md cut list).

## What the docs give us, and what they don't

- Six events, names fixed by marketing ("keep names exactly as written") [D]. Happy path only: no event for a cancel, decline, error or timeout.
- Only `purchase` has params: `transaction_id`, `value`, `currency` [D]. Nothing for the other five (Q20).
- "UTM parameters should survive until `purchase`" [D]. No storage rule, and the flow leaves our origin once or twice: eID, then payment (plus `actionUrl` on `requires_action`). Return can land in another browser (Q7).
- No consent mechanism (Q5). GA4 in the EU needs prior consent for analytics cookies.
- `purchase` fired in the browser misses every user who never comes back from payment, and can fire twice (reload, second tab, second browser).
- The order API returns no amount, currency or trial flag (Q4). `value` is our estimate.

## Module

One pure module, `analytics.ts`:

- `track(event, params)`: typed map of the six events → their params. Unknown event = type error.
- Adds the common params, checks consent, applies the once-rules, then `dataLayer.push`.
- Components and state handlers call `track` on the transitions below. Nothing else touches `dataLayer`.
- Unit-tested: params per event, once-rules, consent gate, no personal data.

## Events

Each event is bound to one transition in 04. Not firing elsewhere is part of the rule.

| Event [D] | Fires on (04) | Params (plus common) | Once-rule [A] |
|---|---|---|---|
| `plan_viewed` | **Entry → Plans** (after `/v1/me` resolves: 200 identified, 401 or 5xx anonymous). Not on Change plan, retry point (reviewStep off), invalid_plan notice, or Entry → Account | `identified` (bool) | Once per document load of Plans via Entry. Reload = new view (GA semantics). bfcache restore (`pageshow.persisted`) re-runs Entry (04 invariant 6) but does not fire |
| `plan_selected` | **Plans —select→** (any target: StartingEid, Review, Gate) | `plan_id` | Every select. Change plan → select again fires again |
| `identity_started` | **StartingEid —201→ redirect to `redirectUrl`**. Not on click (may 429/fail) | `plan_id`, `eid_purpose`: `checkout` \| `reverify` (reverify = orderId in context, from IdentityLost) | Once per 201. Retry after EidFailed/RateLimited fires again: each is a real start |
| `identity_completed` | **Verifying —200→** (any target: Review, Gate, Account, PaymentReturn). Not on `?status=ok` alone: only `/v1/me` proves it | `plan_id`, `eid_purpose` | Once per callback load. EidCallback exits use `history.replace` (04), so Back or reload never re-enters it. Not fired when Entry `/v1/me` 200 skips eID |

### No personal data

Never sent: `customerId`, eID data (none is exposed anyway, Q15), `sessionId`, `paymentUrl`, `actionUrl`, `redirectUrl`, `returnUrl`, error messages. `orderId` is pseudonymous and required by marketing as `transaction_id`. A unit test asserts the param whitelist per event.

## UTM capture and storage

**Capture** [A]: on Entry, read `utm_*` from the landing URL. A new landing with any `utm_*` replaces the whole set (last campaign wins). A landing without UTMs keeps a stored set. Other query params are ignored (`gclid` etc.).

**Carry**: two (three with `actionUrl`) cross-origin redirects, maybe into another browser (Q7).

| Where | Before consent | After consent |
|---|---|---|
| Memory (current page, client-side navigation) | yes | yes |
| `returnUrl` query, eID and payment (Q7) | yes: URL, not storage (Q5) | yes |
| `sessionStorage` (same tab, after a redirect) | no | yes |

Trust order as 04 invariant 2: stored > `returnUrl` query. On return, the app reads UTMs from the query only when nothing is stored. Without consent, UTMs exist only in the URL, so they survive the redirects but not a manual reload of a page without them.

`returnUrl` keeps the standard `utm_*` names. Side effect: the return page view re-states the campaign, so GA4 doesn't credit the eID or payment provider as a referral. Still needed from marketing: eID and payment domains in GA4 "unwanted referrals" (Q47).

Limits: UTMs add to `returnUrl` length, and the provider/API limit is not documented (02). UTMs reach the eID and payment providers in the URL; they hold no personal data.

## Consent

Assumption Q5: GTM Consent Mode v2, basic mode (no Google tags before consent). CMP vendor unknown.

| | Before a decision | Granted (`analytics_storage`) | Denied or withdrawn |
|---|---|---|---|
| Consent default | `gtag('consent', 'default', {analytics_storage, ad_storage, ad_user_data, ad_personalization: 'denied'})` before GTM loads | `update` by the CMP | stays denied |
| App events | Queued in memory, current page only | Queue flushed, then pushed live | Queue dropped, nothing pushed |
| UTMs | Memory + URL | + `sessionStorage` | Memory + URL. Withdrawal clears our keys |
| `purchase` guard | not written | `localStorage` | not written. Withdrawal keeps existing keys (orderId only, no personal data), so a re-grant + reload can't send `purchase` twice |
| GA cookies (`_ga`) | none | set by GA | none |

- Queued events not flushed before a redirect or reload are lost. Accepted (Q5): a user who decides after eID shows `identity_completed` without `plan_viewed`/`plan_selected`/`identity_started`, so the top of the funnel is undercounted.
- Return in another browser: no CMP cookie there, so the banner shows again on the callback page; events queue until the decision.
- The flow never waits for, or depends on, consent or GTM. Functional storage (open order, attempt marker, Q37) is not analytics and needs no consent.
- Advanced mode (cookieless pings) is a Legal decision (Q5).
- The CMP and GTM count against LCP, INP and CLS on Plans, not the JS size budget (08).

| Gap | Effect | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| User never returns from payment (closes tab, Unconfirmed → "Go to account", provider return fails) | `purchase` never sent, revenue undercounted | Server-side `purchase` (cut, PLAN.md) |
| Return in another tab or browser | Guard is per browser: a second browser can send `purchase` again. GA4 drops a repeated `transaction_id` only for the same user | Server-side `purchase` (cut) |
| Return in another browser | New GA client id: `purchase` attributed to a new user, campaign only from `returnUrl` UTMs | Server-side `purchase` (cut) |
| Consent denied | No events at all | Accepted (Legal) |

| `value` is an estimate | Can differ from what was charged | Amount on the order (Q4) |

## Checks

Every expectation below names its check. No check = not an expectation.

- **unit**: Vitest + Testing Library, next to the module.
- **e2e**: Playwright against the mock (`MOCK_TIME_SCALE=50`).
- **axe**: `@axe-core/playwright` inside e2e, rules `wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21aa, wcag22aa`, zero violations. New dev dependency: automated WCAG checks on every screen, the only way to cover all of them in CI.
- **Lighthouse**: Lighthouse CI, mobile preset (mid-range phone, 4× CPU throttle, slow 4G), median of 3 runs on the static build. New dev dependency: budgets fail the build.
- **build**: a script in `next build` (no dependency).
- **manual**: release checklist, VoiceOver iOS Safari + TalkBack Android Chrome, before each market launch.

**In the slice**: unit, e2e (happy path + `payment_declined`, PLAN 2.7) with axe on every screen they reach. **Post-slice**: Lighthouse, build scripts, fallback e2e (needs the built `out/` behind a static server that serves `404.html`; `next dev` routes differently; `resolvePair` is unit-tested in the slice), axe on the other states, manual.

70 % of traffic on phones, "under two minutes" [D brief], no budgets (Q22). Budgets apply to the Plans page (entry, where most users bounce), on the Lighthouse mobile preset.

| Metric | Budget | Check |
|---|---|---|
| LCP | < 2.5 s | Lighthouse |
| CLS | < 0.1 | Lighthouse; e2e: no layout shift entry > 0 after `/v1/me` resolves |
| INP | < 200 ms. Lab proxy: TBT < 200 ms | Lighthouse (TBT). Field INP not measured (cut, PLAN.md) |
| JS | ≤ 150 KB gzip first load on Plans, our code + framework. GTM and CMP excluded here (loaded after hydration) but included in LCP, INP, CLS. Framework alone is roughly 85–100 KB (estimate): measure at scaffold (PLAN 2.1) | build (sum of route chunks) |
| Flow time | `plan_viewed` → `purchase` median < 2 min | GA (after launch, 07) |

### What Plans may wait for

- **Nothing at runtime for first paint.** Headline, cards and prices are in the HTML (CMS + `/v1/plans` at build, Q23). Check: e2e with the API blocked → cards and prices visible.
- `/v1/me` runs after hydration and never blocks paint. Trial copy is only on Review (04), so its answer moves nothing on Plans. An active subscriber sees Plans briefly, then redirects (Q10). Check: e2e.
- Resume banner (open order) is a sticky overlay, not inserted above the cards. Check: e2e CLS entry.
- GTM and CMP load `afterInteractive`; the banner is an overlay, never the LCP element. Check: manual read of the Lighthouse LCP element (`<h1>` or first card).
- Fonts: system stack, or one self-hosted font with `font-display: swap` + `size-adjust`. No hero image. Check: Lighthouse.

### How SSG closes the gap

Each pair is static HTML on the CDN: low TTFB, LCP element in the first response, no client fetch before paint. The remaining cost is hydration, so Plans is a server component; only the select buttons and the flow controller are client code. Polling, Review and callbacks are their own routes, split out of the Plans bundle. Check: build (JS budget), Lighthouse.
# Nordlight mock server

A convenience built from the API notes in `docs/02-api-notes.md`. Where the notes are silent, the mock had to make a choice. The real services may differ, so treat anything you rely on here as an assumption to write down.

Everything is in memory. Restart the server, or `POST /__mock/reset`, to start clean.

## Choosing a scenario

A scenario decides how the mock behaves. Pick one in any of these ways. The first match wins:

1. The `x-scenario` request header.
2. A `?scenario=` query parameter. This also sets a `nl_scenario` cookie, so the choice sticks for later requests, including page navigations to the fake providers.
3. The `nl_scenario` cookie, which you can also set by clicking a scenario on the landing page (<http://localhost:4010>).
4. Otherwise `happy`.

When you create an identity session or an order, the mock remembers the scenario in force at that moment and uses it for the provider pages that follow.

| Scenario | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `happy` | Everything works. Payment is confirmed about 3 seconds after the customer pays. |
| `identity_cancelled` | The customer cancels at the eID provider. |
| `identity_slow` | The eID provider takes about 8 seconds to answer. |
| `rate_limited` | `POST /v1/identity/sessions` answers 429 with a `Retry-After` header. |
| `already_subscribed` | `GET /v1/me` reports an active subscription. |
| `not_trial_eligible` | `GET /v1/me` reports `trialEligible: false`. |
| `payment_declined` | The payment provider declines the payment. |
| `payment_slow` | Payment is confirmed about 45 seconds after the customer pays. |
| `payment_requires_action` | The provider asks for an extra authentication step before it confirms payment. |
| `api_500` | Every `/v1` endpoint except `GET /v1/plans` answers 500. |

## Endpoints

| Endpoint | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/plans?market=EE` | Markets: `EE`, `LV`, `LT`. Returns `{ market, plans: [{ id, name, priceNet, vatRate, currency }] }`. |
| `POST /v1/identity/sessions` | Optional body `{ "returnUrl": "..." }`. Defaults to `WEB_ORIGIN/auth/callback`. Returns `{ sessionId, redirectUrl }`. |
| `GET /v1/me` | Needs the session cookie. Returns `{ customerId, activeSubscription, trialEligible }`. |
| `POST /v1/orders` | Body `{ "planId": "plan_std_m", "returnUrl": "..." }`. `returnUrl` is optional and defaults to `WEB_ORIGIN/payment/return`. Returns `{ orderId, paymentUrl }`. |
| `GET /v1/orders/{id}` | Returns `{ orderId, planId, status, createdAt }`. When the status is `requires_action` it also returns `actionUrl`. |
| `GET /cms/v1/plan-pages?market=EE&locale=et` | The CMS entry for a market and language. The same data is in `fixtures/cms/`. |

Return URLs must be on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, or the configured `WEB_ORIGIN`.

## The fake providers

These are plain HTML pages that continue automatically after a short delay, with buttons if you want to click through by hand.

- **eID** at `/mock-eid/{sessionId}`. When it finishes, it sets the session cookie on success and sends the browser to your `returnUrl` with `?status=ok`, `?status=cancelled` or `?status=expired`.
- **Payment** at `/mock-pay/{orderId}`. When it finishes, it sends the browser to your order's `returnUrl` with `?orderId=...`, plus `&cancelled=1` if the customer pressed Cancel.

Payment results arrive separately, as they would from a webhook. Check the order status through the API.

Browsers on `localhost` share cookies across ports, so your app on `localhost:3000` can use the cookie the mock sets on `localhost:4010`.

## Debugging

- `GET /__mock/state` shows sessions, customers and orders as the mock sees them.
- `POST /__mock/reset` clears everything.
- Each request is logged to the console with its scenario and status code.
- CORS is enabled with credentials for `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` origins. Add more with `ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://a.example,https://b.example`.

And English formatting: `en` alone gives US style ("December 10, 2026", "€11.15"). | Marketing + Product | We write `en`, other catalogs translated before launch. `en` formats as `en-150` ("10 December 2026"). |

# Senior Frontend Assignment: Spec-Driven Checkout

Thank you for continuing with us. This assignment mirrors how we want to work: a product idea arrives half-finished, and you turn it into a spec that people and AI coding tools can build from safely.

## The scenario

Nordlight is a fictional video streaming service in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Product wants a new web flow where a visitor chooses a plan, identifies themselves with a national eID, pays, and lands in the app as a subscriber. The product brief, API notes, CMS content model and analytics notes are in `docs/`. They are realistic, which means they are incomplete and not fully consistent with each other.

Engineering plans to build this feature mostly with AI coding tools. Your job is to write the spec that makes that possible, then prove it works.

## What to deliver

1. **The spec (about 60% of your effort).** Markdown files in the `spec/` folder. It must cover:
   - scope and non-goals;
   - the systems the frontend depends on and the systems that depend on it;
   - assumptions and open questions, each with who should answer;
   - the user flow as a state machine, including failure and recovery;
   - what you need from the API and the CMS;
   - analytics, i18n, accessibility and performance expectations;
   - a test strategy;
   - rollout and monitoring;
   - a breakdown into work items small enough for an AI tool to complete in one session, each with acceptance criteria.
2. **A thin slice (about 30%).** A working frontend of the flow from plan selection to confirmation against the mock server, in `app/`. Cover the happy path and at least two failure paths of your choice. Build it with AI tools, driven by your spec. Include unit tests and at least one end-to-end test.
3. **An AI working log** (`AI-LOG.md`). What you asked the tools to do, how you structured the context you gave them, and at least three specific places where the output was wrong or weak and what you did about it. A curated one to two pages is enough; raw transcripts are welcome as an appendix.
4. **A note to the team** (`TEAM-NOTE.md`, one page, about 10%). Written to the product lead and the backend lead: the five questions or risks that matter most, and your recommendation on each.

## Ground rules

- **Time.** Plan on 4 to 5 hours and stop at 5. Tell us what you cut. A sharp spec with a small slice beats the reverse.
- **AI use is expected.** Use any tools you like and tell us which. You are accountable for everything you submit, including what the tools wrote.
- **Stack.** TypeScript with a component framework you know well (Vue or Nuxt, React or Next, or similar). No real provider integrations; use the mock server in `mock-server/`.
- **Questions.** You may send up to three questions to your recruiter contact. We reply within one working day. Good questions count in your favour.
- **Submission.** A git repository or zip with a README that explains how to run everything, the spec, the log and the note.

## What happens next

We read your submission, then spend 60 minutes together walking through it. Expect us to ask why you made specific choices and what you would do differently with another week.

# 09 · Test strategy

What each test level proves, where each mock scenario is tested, how E2E runs. States: 04. Error kinds: 05. Events: 07. Check names (unit, e2e, axe): 08. Q-numbers: 03.

## Levels

| Level | Tool | Proves | Runs in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit: domain | Vitest | Price (Q2) per locale, planKey map (Q11), trial rule (Q12), `resolvePair`, plurals and tags (08), catalogs share keys | `npm test`, every commit |
| Unit: state machine | Vitest `test.each` | One case per exit in 04 States and Gate: (state, event) → next state + effects. Invariants as their own cases: only Pay / Try again creates an order (1), no error kind leads to PaymentFailed (3), every non-terminal state has an exit (4) | same |
| Unit: adapters | Vitest | `toApiError`: both shapes, non-JSON, network, `Retry-After` + 30 s fallback; one case per row of the 05 kind table. Zod schemas parse mock responses (`fixtures/`), reject drift. `returnUrl` build ↔ parse round trip (Q7) | same |
| Unit: polling | Vitest fake timers | 2 s → 20 s → 5 s → 3 min (Q9), "Still confirming" at 20 s, Unconfirmed at 3 min, 5xx keeps polling, `requires_action` redirects once per cycle | same |
| Unit: analytics | Vitest | Params per event, whitelist, once-rules, consent gate (07) | post-slice (07 is out of slice) |
| Component | Vitest + Testing Library | Each 04 screen rendered from a state: focus on `<h1>`, live region text changes only on state change, in-flight button (two clicks → one request), buttons per state (Resume hides Pay), synthetic `pageshow` re-runs on-enter (inv. 6) | same |
| E2E | Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright` | Real redirects and cookies across ports, context from `returnUrl`, rehydration on reload and cross-origin return, one order per attempt, zero axe violations per screen reached | `npm run e2e`, before merge |
| Contract | — | Real API matches Zod schemas and 05 | later: no real API yet (Q6, Q43) |

Notes on the levels:

- **State machine cases come from 04, not from the code.** The expected (state, event → next) list is written by hand from 04; the machine is the subject. Generating cases from the machine's own table would test nothing.
- **E2E doesn't catch every rehydration bug.** It covers reload and return from a provider. Playwright may not hit bfcache (08), so Back-restore is covered by the component `pageshow` case + manual.
- **`MOCK_TIME_SCALE` speeds up the mock, not the app.** Poll thresholds, the `Retry-After` countdown and redirect delays are app timers: unit tests use fake timers, E2E uses `page.clock`.

## Scenario matrix

Unit/component cases for every row are in the slice. **Cut order** applies to the E2E part: `S` = in the slice (PLAN 2.7), never cut; numbers = post-slice, `1` dropped first (PLAN cut list first, then lowest risk).

| Scenario | Variant | Level | Asserts | Cut order |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `happy` | Anonymous, full path | E2E | Plans → eID → Review (trial note on Standard) → pay → Confirmed with order id. One order in `/__mock/state`. axe on each screen, unique `document.title` | S |
| `happy` | Back from pay page to Review | E2E | Resume: "Continue payment" reuses `paymentUrl`, Pay hidden, still one order | 13 |
| `happy` | Storage cleared before return | E2E | Plan, market, locale, `lang` from the `returnUrl` query (inv. 2, 5) | 12 |
| `happy` | Cookie cleared before return | E2E | eID return → OtherBrowser; payment return → IdentityLost, no new order | 11 |
| `happy` | Cancel on pay page | E2E | PaymentFailed(cancelled) banner; Try again → new orderId | 9 |
| `happy` | Reload on Confirmed | E2E | Still Confirmed, no trial note, no second order | 8 |
| `happy` | Double tap, reload in CreatingOrder, second tab | unit, component | One request; marker → "last attempt didn't finish"; Gate → Resume | S (no E2E) |
| `payment_declined` | — | E2E | Polling → PaymentFailed(declined) at retry point; Try again → second orderId ≠ first | S |
| `identity_cancelled` | — | unit, E2E | EidFailed(cancelled); Try again → new eID session, plan kept | 5 |
| `identity_cancelled` | Expired: reopen used `/mock-eid/{id}/complete` | unit, E2E | EidFailed(expired); missing/unknown `status` → expired (unit only) | 5 |
| `identity_slow` | — | E2E | Same as `happy`; nothing in the app times out during the provider wait | 2 |
| `rate_limited` | — | unit, E2E | RateLimited, countdown from `Retry-After: 30`; live region gets 2 messages; Try again enabled after `page.clock.runFor(30_000)` | 6 |
| `already_subscribed` | Anonymous, after eID | unit, E2E | Verifying → `ACCOUNT_URL` (stubbed with `page.route`) | 10 |
| `already_subscribed` | Identified at Entry; 409 on order | unit, E2E | Entry → Account (cookie switched after eID); 409 → Account (unit only) | 10 |
| `not_trial_eligible` | — | E2E | Review: full price, no trial note on Standard | 3 |
| `payment_slow` | — | unit, E2E | "Still confirming" after `page.clock` passes 20 s; then Confirmed | 7 |
| `payment_requires_action` | Approve | E2E | Challenge → Approve → Confirmed | 1 |

I wrote `spec/09-test-strategy.md` (78 lines). It has the levels table, the scenario matrix with all 10 mock scenarios plus the main non-scenario cases, the E2E setup, and what isn't tested. I kept your approach and changed four things in it:

- **State machine tests:** I wrote the expected cases by hand from 04 instead of generating them. If they were generated from the machine's own transition table, they would only check the machine against itself.
- **"Only E2E catches rehydration":** that holds for reload and return from the providers, but not for Back. Playwright may not restore pages from the back-forward cache (08 says so too). Back-restore is covered by a component test that fires a fake `pageshow` event, plus a manual check.
- **`MOCK_TIME_SCALE` doesn't touch the app's timers.** It only speeds up the mock's delays. The 20 s "Still confirming", the 3 min cutoff, the 30 s `Retry-After` countdown and the redirect delay all run on the app's own clock. Unit tests use fake timers; E2E uses Playwright's `page.clock`.
- **E2E runs on one worker.** The mock keeps all its state in one shared store, so a `POST /__mock/reset` from one test would wipe another test's orders if they ran in parallel.

Other choices you may want to change:
- **Scenario selection:** E2E picks the scenario with an `nl_scenario` cookie, not the `x-scenario` header. The cookie also reaches the provider pages, and the app never has to send test headers.
- **Expiry:** the mock doesn't speed up the 5 min eID or 1 h session lifetimes. Tests fake them by reusing a completed eID session or clearing cookies.
- **Cut order:** the 14 post-slice E2E items start with the PLAN cut list, then drop the lowest-risk ones first. "`api_500` after eID" and "Back from the pay page" are kept to the end.
- **Analytics unit tests:** listed as post-slice, since 07 is out of the slice.

**Mismatch:** PLAN.md 1.10 names the file `09-testing.md`. I used your name, so PLAN or the spec README should be updated to match.

content.text:
Six problems below. The first two would break or quietly weaken slice tests, so they matter most.

**04 invariants with no test**
- **Inv. 2 (trust order):** every case has only one source of context. No test has stored context and the URL query disagree, so an app that always reads the URL passes. No test checks that `cancelled=1` is only a hint: e.g. `cancelled=1` while the server says `paid` or `pending` should not show PaymentFailed.
- **Inv. 5 (context survives redirects):**
  - Nothing asserts that `utm_*` is in the `returnUrl`.
  - The orderId carried through IdentityLost → Verify → PaymentReturn is never followed. The "cookie cleared" row stops at IdentityLost.
- **Inv. 6 (re-derive on every show):** the `pageshow` component case checks that on-enter runs again. It doesn't check that disabled buttons are re-enabled on restore.
- **EidCallback `history.replace` (04 rule, not numbered):** no test that Back or reload after the callback doesn't re-run it.

**E2E rows that pass with the bug still there, or can't run as written**
- **The mock providers continue on their own.** The pay, challenge and eID pages auto-continue after 1.5 s ÷ 50 = 30 ms. That beats a test's click, so "click buttons, never wait" doesn't hold.

# 09 · Test strategy

What each test level proves, where each mock scenario is tested, how E2E runs. States: 04. Error kinds: 05. Events: 07. Check names (unit, e2e, axe): 08. Q-numbers: 03.

**Slice** = what PLAN 2.4–2.6 builds: Plans, eID start + callback (ok, cancelled, expired, 429, already subscribed), Review, order, payment return, Polling, Confirmed, PaymentFailed(declined), `requires_action`. Not in the slice: Gate (open order, attempt marker, Resume), OtherBrowser, IdentityLost, OrderNotFound, PaymentFailed(cancelled), the `api_500` states (StartError, VerifyError, Unconfirmed), UTM carry, analytics.

## Levels

| Level | Tool | Proves | Runs in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Unit: domain | Vitest | Price (Q2) per locale, planKey map (Q11), trial rule (Q12), `resolvePair`, plurals and tags (08), catalogs share keys | `npm test`, every commit |
| Unit: state machine | Vitest `test.each` | One case per exit in 04 States and Gate: (state, event) → next state + effects. Invariants as their own cases: only Pay / Try again creates an order (1); stored context beats a conflicting query, query used only when nothing is stored, `cancelled=1` loses to server `paid`/`pending` (2); no error kind leads to PaymentFailed (3); every non-terminal state has an exit (4) | same. Slice states in the slice, the rest post-slice |
| Unit: adapters | Vitest | `toApiError`: both shapes, non-JSON, network, `Retry-After` + 30 s fallback; one case per row of the 05 kind table. Zod schemas parse sample bodies copied from 05/mock and `fixtures/cms/`, reject drift. `returnUrl` build ↔ parse round trip: plan, market, locale (slice), `utm_*`, `orderId` (post-slice) (inv. 5) | same |
| Unit: polling | Vitest fake timers | 2 s → 20 s → 5 s → 3 min (Q9), "Still confirming" at 20 s, Unconfirmed at 3 min, 5xx keeps polling, `requires_action` redirects once per cycle | same |
| Unit: analytics | Vitest | Params per event, whitelist, once-rules, consent gate (07) | post-slice |
| Component | Vitest + Testing Library | Each 04 screen rendered from a state: focus on `<h1>`, live region text changes only on state change, in-flight button (two clicks → one request), buttons per state. Synthetic `pageshow` (persisted): on-enter runs again and disabled buttons are enabled again (inv. 6) | same as state machine |
| E2E | Playwright + `@axe-core/playwright` | Real redirects and cookies across ports, context from `returnUrl`, rehydration on reload and cross-origin return, one order per attempt, zero axe violations per screen reached | `npm run e2e`, before merge |
| Contract | — | Real API matches Zod schemas and 05 | later: no real API yet (Q6, Q43) |

- **State machine cases come from 04, not from the code.** The expected (state, event → next) list is written by hand from 04, and the machine is what's tested. Cases generated from the machine's own table would test nothing.
- **E2E doesn't catch every rehydration bug.** It covers reload and return from a provider. Playwright may not hit bfcache (08), so Back-restore = component `pageshow` case + manual.
- **`MOCK_TIME_SCALE` speeds up the mock, not the app.** Poll thresholds and the `Retry-After` countdown are app timers: fake timers in unit, `page.clock` in E2E.

## Scenario matrix

**Cut order**: `S` = unit + E2E in the slice, never cut. `U·n` = unit in the slice, E2E post-slice. `n` = whole row post-slice. `U` / `P` = unit only, in / after the slice. E2E `1` is dropped first (PLAN cut list first, then lowest risk). Negative asserts ("absent", "no …") run only after the positive anchor named first in the cell.

| Scenario | Variant | Level | Asserts | Cut order |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `happy` | Anonymous, full path | E2E | Plans → eID → Review (trial note on Standard) → pay → Confirmed with order id; then exactly one order in `/__mock/state`. axe on each screen, unique `document.title` | S |
| `happy` | Back after eID callback | E2E | Review visible → `goBack()` → URL is not `/auth/callback` (04 `history.replace`) | 6 |
| `happy` | Stored context vs tampered query | E2E | Return URL with another plan/market → Review shows the stored plan and market | U·13 |
| `happy` | Storage cleared before return | E2E | Plan, market, locale, `lang` from the `returnUrl` query (inv. 2, 5) | U·14 |
| `happy` | `cancelled=1` on a paid order | E2E | Open `/payment/return?orderId={paid}&cancelled=1` → Confirmed, no failure banner | U·12 |
| `happy` | Callback in a new context (no cookie) | E2E | `/auth/callback?status=ok&…` → OtherBrowser; "Start again here" keeps the query's plan | 15 |
| `happy` | Cookie cleared before payment return | E2E | IdentityLost with order id → Verify: eID `returnUrl` carries `orderId` → PaymentReturn → OrderNotFound (mock: new customer, 04); order count still 1 | 16 |
| `happy` | Back from pay page to Review | E2E | "Continue payment" visible and reuses `paymentUrl` → Pay absent → order count still 1 | 17 |
| `happy` | Cancel on pay page | E2E | PaymentFailed(cancelled) banner → Try again → second pay page with a new orderId, order count 2 | 9 |
| `happy` | Reload on Confirmed | E2E | Order id visible again → no trial note, order count still 1 | U·8 |
| `happy` | Landing with `utm_*` | E2E | `utm_*` + plan, market, locale in both `returnUrl` request bodies (`page.waitForRequest`) | 7 |
| `happy` | Double tap on Pay | unit, component | Two clicks → one request, focus unchanged | U |
| `happy` | Reload in CreatingOrder, second tab | unit | Marker → "last attempt didn't finish"; open order in shared storage → Resume | P |
| `payment_declined` | — | E2E | Polling → PaymentFailed(declined) at retry point → Try again → second pay page with a new orderId, order count 2 | S |
| `identity_cancelled` | — | unit, E2E | EidFailed(cancelled); Try again → new eID session, plan kept | U·4 |
| `identity_cancelled` | Expired: reopen used `/mock-eid/{id}/complete` | unit, E2E | EidFailed(expired); missing/unknown `status` → expired (unit only) | U·4 |
| `identity_slow` | — | E2E | Same as `happy` full path | 2 |
| `rate_limited` | — | unit, E2E | RateLimited, countdown from `Retry-After: 30`; live region gets 2 messages; Try again enabled after `runFor(30_000)` | U·5 |
| `already_subscribed` | Anonymous, after eID | unit, E2E | Verifying → `ACCOUNT_URL` (stubbed with `page.route`) | U·10 |
| `already_subscribed` | Identified at Entry; 409 on order | unit, E2E | Entry → Account (cookie switched after eID); 409 → Account (unit only) | U·10 |
| `not_trial_eligible` | — | unit, E2E | Review full price visible → no trial note on Standard | U·3 |
| `payment_slow` | — | unit, E2E | Polling reached (status in live region) → "Still confirming" after `runFor(20_000)` → Confirmed | S |
| `payment_requires_action` | Approve | E2E | Challenge → Approve → Confirmed | U·1 |
| `payment_requires_action` | Leave challenge, open return URL | unit, E2E | Polling sees `requires_action` → one redirect to `actionUrl` → Fail → PaymentFailed(declined) | U·1 |
| `api_500` | Anonymous | unit, E2E | Plans + prices visible (build data); Entry → anonymous; StartingEid → StartError with Try again | 11 |
| `api_500` | Gate, cookie switched on Review | unit, E2E | Pay → retry point error visible → no `POST /v1/orders` request sent (Gate step 3 `/v1/me` 500) | 18 |
| `api_500` | Polling: `happy` order, cookie switched before return | unit, E2E | "Connection issue" visible → Unconfirmed after `runFor(180_000)` with order id → no PaymentFailed (inv. 3) | 19 |

## E2E setup

- **Ports.** Mock `http://localhost:4010`, app `http://localhost:3000`. Always `localhost`, because cookies are shared across ports only there. The mock's default `WEB_ORIGIN` is the app origin.
- **Servers.** Playwright `webServer`: mock (`MOCK_TIME_SCALE=50`) first, then the app, since the build reads `/v1/plans` (Q23). Slice: `next dev`. Post-slice: built `out/` behind a static server (08 fallback).
- **Serial.** `workers: 1`. The mock keeps all state in one in-memory store, so a parallel test's reset would wipe another test's orders.
- **Reset.** `POST /__mock/reset` in `beforeEach` via Playwright `request`. Each test gets a fresh browser context, so no storage or cookies carry over.
- **Scenario.** `context.addCookies([{ name: 'nl_scenario', value, domain: 'localhost', path: '/' }])` before the first navigation. It reaches app fetches and provider pages; the mock pins the scenario to each eID session and order at creation. Switching mid-test = add the cookie again. The app never sends `x-scenario`.
- **Clock.** `page.clock.install()` before the first navigation in every test. Provider pages auto-continue after 30 ms at scale 50, which would beat a click, so their timers stay frozen and tests click the provider buttons. App timers advance with `runFor`. Mock settle delays run on server time: wait for them in an `expect.poll` that calls `runFor(5_000)` per try.
- **No sleeps.** No `waitForTimeout`. Wait on `waitForURL` and web-first assertions (`toHaveText`, `toBeVisible`, live region text).
- **Not scaled by the mock**: eID TTL 5 min and session 1 h. Expiry is simulated by reusing a completed eID session or `context.clearCookies()`.
- **Order count**: `GET /__mock/state`, read only after the anchor in the row (Confirmed, Resume, second pay page).
- **axe**: `AxeBuilder` with the 08 tags once each screen settles (after `<h1>` has focus). **On failure**: trace and screenshot kept.

## Not tested, and why

| What | Why | Instead |
|---|---|---|
| Real API, eID, payment | Not available; the mock is the assumed contract (Q6) | Contract tests later |
| bfcache restore in E2E | Playwright may not restore from bfcache | Component `pageshow` case, manual (08) |
| A real second browser / app switch | Can't be driven from one Playwright context | New context, cleared storage or cookies |
| Wall-clock eID / session expiry | Mock doesn't scale them | Reused session, cleared cookie |
| Network loss on `POST /v1/orders` (Q34) | Mock can't drop a response | Unit with a rejecting fetch |
| Two tabs POSTing in the same instant | Unpreventable without `Idempotency-Key` (Q19) | Unit: Gate reads shared storage |
| LV pages | `market.LV` off (Q13) | Build check (08), post-slice |
| GA4 delivery, GTM, CMP | Out of slice; delivery only visible in GA | Unit on `analytics.ts`; DebugView manual |
| Lighthouse, screen readers, non-text contrast | Post-slice or not automatable | 08 checks |
| Visual regression | No design baseline | — |

+- **Clock.** `page.clock.install()` before the first navigation in every test. Provider pages auto-continue after 30 ms at scale 50, which would beat a click, so their timers stay frozen and tests click the provider buttons. App timers advance with `runFor`. Mock settle delays run on server time: wait for them in an `expect.poll` that calls `runFor(5_000)` per try.

- **Not scaled by the mock**: eID TTL 5 min and session 1 h. Expiry is simulated by reusing a completed eID session or `context.clearCookies()`.

I fixed all findings in `spec/09-testing.md`, which is now 84 lines. Nothing has run yet, since there are no tests in `app/` so far.

**Your two decisions:**
- **`payment_slow` is now in the slice.** With a ~0.9 s settle, it's the only slice E2E that reliably reaches Polling. I also updated PLAN 2.7 and the slice line in `spec/08-quality.md` to match.
- **Slice scope shrunk to what PLAN 2.4–2.6 builds.** A new "Slice" paragraph lists what's in and out. The double-tap, reload-in-CreatingOrder and second-tab row is split: the double-tap guard stays a slice unit test, the other two become post-slice unit tests. The cut-order column now has five codes: `S` (unit + E2E in slice, never cut), `U·n` (unit in slice, E2E post-slice), `n` (whole row post-slice), `U` (unit only, in slice), `P` (unit only, post-slice).

**One decision I made without asking:** every E2E test installs `page.clock` before its first navigation. This freezes the provider pages' auto-continue so tests can click the buttons. App timers are moved forward with `runFor`. The mock's own settle delays run on server time, so tests wait for them with an `expect.poll` loop.

**Invariants now covered:**
- **Inv. 2:** a unit case where stored context beats a conflicting query, and one where `cancelled=1` loses to server `paid`/`pending`. Two new E2E rows: a tampered return query, and `cancelled=1` on a paid order.
- **Inv. 5:** the `returnUrl` round trip now includes `utm_*` and `orderId`. New E2E rows check the UTMs in both request bodies and follow the IdentityLost → Verify → OrderNotFound path.
- **Inv. 6:** the `pageshow` component case now also checks that disabled buttons are enabled again.
- **`history.replace`:** a new E2E row checks that Back after the eID callback doesn't return to `/auth/callback`.

**E2E rows that could pass with the bug still there:**
- **Negative asserts** now run only after a positive anchor, as a rule in the legend and spelled out in each cell.
- **The eID "no cookie" case** now opens the callback in a new browser context. The payment part still clears cookies before the return.
- **`api_500` Gate** now asserts that no order request is sent, instead of counting orders.
- **`api_500` Polling** now starts from a `happy` order and switches the scenario before the return.
- **`payment_declined` and cancel** now read the order count only on the second pay page.
